author: Swinhoe, 1867
summary: 해안 앞바다의 섬에 살며 일부 지역에서는 흔한 여름철새이다. 섬의 바위틈이나 슴새가 쓰던 땅굴, 또는 스스로 판 깊이 1m에 이르는 땅굴에 둥지를 틀고, 흰 알 1개를 암수가 함께 품는다. 국내에서는 서해안과 독도에 살며, 국외로는 일본의 섬들과 중국, 타이완, 싱가포르, 수마트라, 자바, 인도양에 분포한다.

art.subject: Swinhoe's Storm Petrel (Hydrobates monorhis), adult in summer (breeding season around Korean offshore islands): whole plumage dark sooty brown, the head the same colour as the body; on each upperwing a paler greyish-brown diagonal band across the coverts from the bend of the wing; primaries, secondaries and tail blackish; underparts and underwing dark greyish-brown with no white anywhere; rump dark, the same colour as the back; tail blackish and forked; small black bill with a tube-shaped nostril on top; dark eye; black legs and feet.
art.pose: flying low over the sea, wings spread
art.scene: Korean summer sea beside a rocky offshore island; no people, buildings or text
views: adult in flight seen from above, head, body and tail in line: all dark sooty-brown body and rump, blackish flight feathers, a paler greyish-brown diagonal band across each upperwing, forked blackish tail
adult, side view crouching low on rock at a burrow entrance: small dark sooty-brown bird resting on short black legs, tube-nosed black bill, long folded wings, blackish forked tail
art.build: Small seabird, about 20cm: about the length of a Barn Swallow but with longer, broader, angled wings. Small rounded head, short neck, slender body. Bill short and black, much shorter than the head, with a raised tubular nostril on the upper mandible and a small hooked tip. Legs short, thin and black; in flight the feet do not project beyond the tail. Wings long and pointed, sharply bent at the wrist. Tail moderately forked. Flies low over the sea with buoyant, bounding flight and erratic changes of direction.
avoid: Do not paint a white rump; Swinhoe's Storm Petrel has a dark rump, unlike Leach's Storm Petrel.
Do not paint a swallow: no glossy blue and no red throat, and the bill has a tubular nostril.
Do not paint white underparts or a white band on the underwing.
Do not paint long legs or feet trailing beyond the tail.
